items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-07-31
items.q: you probably were reading Paul Edward Miller

ctx.x: I'd never heard of downbeat except I don't think I'd ever heard of downbeat at all I know that in the early 40s I would read Esquire yeah which somehow or other I took to be the the arbeiter of of taste for men anyway mm-hmm and besides of course being interested in looking at the petty girl pictures I don't remember whether they had a centerfold or whether it was or quite what it was that was where the petty girls were and I'd read their articles in fact I'd read the whole damn magazine which I always did at…

accelerating it well I don't know somehow I found downbeat on the newsstands I think starting something in 1943 and uh of course I got disagreed with some of the writers tremendously the same experience you had you probably were reading Paul Edward Miller and Ash Quire yeah I'm sure I read Ash Quire too anyhow uh Mr. Orrin had all kind of things around that shop it wasn't just uh records that we could go in and listen to by the hour without ever buying one

well well interestingly I never heard of the shop until until probably the spring of 1948 at which time uh the class uh my roommate up at Ellisview Johnny Scyther whose picture incidentally is in one of the uh Ottoman tea room uh photographs uh with uh Stuart Bergen's band uh brought up some records that he bought there and uh wasn't until the following fall however that I first went down there but I didn't you know I had not heard that there was it was such a place before that of course I obviously enough was a…
